product-promise.description: The task primarily changes the product promise or expected user outcome.

scientific-evidence.description: The task primarily researches, verifies, or appraises scientific evidence and its uncertainty.

user-experience.description: The task primarily changes the intended user journey, interaction, content, accessibility, or design system.

repository-behavior.description: The task primarily changes or repairs repository behavior and implementation quality.

production-state.description: The task primarily changes deployment, runtime configuration, observability, capacity, or production reliability.

production-incident.description: The task primarily detects, mitigates, verifies, or learns from a production incident.

agent-system.description: The task primarily evaluates agents, prompts, routing, review effort, policy, or autonomy.

product-value.description: The task contains a user-value, priority, scope, product-promise, or outcome decision.

scientific-evidence-or-claim.description: The task changes a scientific claim, formula, constant, model, applicability boundary, or safety interpretation.

user-visible-experience.description: The task changes user-visible behavior, interaction, content, accessibility, or rendered experience.

repository-change.description: The authorized action edits repository code, configuration, tests, workflows, or durable documentation; unrelated findings do not expand its scope.

production-operation.description: The authorized action changes or executes deployment, runtime configuration, monitoring, capacity, rollback, or recovery, including actual automatic deployment side effects of a merge. Classify the causal effect of this action, not an unrelated production incident.

incident-response.description: The authorized action responds to an active or recently mitigated production incident; an unrelated incident is a separate task unless a causal safety dependency connects it.

agent-policy-or-autonomy.description: The task changes agent roles, prompts, models, routing, evaluation, review policy, or autonomy.

architecture-boundary.description: The task crosses a service, datastore, domain, repository, irreversible migration, or material non-functional boundary.

trust-boundary.description: The task changes security, privacy, identity, authorization, sensitive data, dependencies, or supply-chain trust.
